title: DAC sum, voice filter, shaper and polarity
author: MrScruff (rytm-mods); elemod port: Iced-Cream
description: All eight voices leave the analog main bus and reach it again through the DAC, panned and summed on the ColdFire: the groundwork for processing a voice after its analog filter, such as a digital filter. The route mask store in the audio interrupt sets every voice's main-disable bit. After the receive buffer fills, each voice slot - the voice after its analog filter and amp, before pan - is split by the pan of its VCA words, as 0006 does, and the two sums are added to the PRE return pair of the output ring, which enters the analog mix ahead of the master distortion and compressor. A voice whose track stock has off the main bus stays out of the sum. The cost is fixed per block; nothing stands aside. Each voice is filtered first, set on a second FILTER page, DAC FILTER, reached by pressing FILTER again while DAC SUM is on. Its top row is FRQ, RES, TYP and DEP; stock's FILTER graph is drawn over FRQ and RES from FRQ, TYP and (for the 2-pole types) RES, a flat line when TYP is OFF. TYP runs in stock's FILTER order - OFF, LP2, LP1, BP, HP1, HP2, BS, PK - and shows stock's TYP glyph and popup, or OFF. LP1 and HP1 are a bilinear first-order section (6 dB/oct, exactly -3 dB at the cutoff); the others a biquad each (the RBJ cookbook's sections, BP with 0 dB at the centre, BS the notch). FRQ is stock's FRQ scale, a semitone a step with 440 Hz at 60, and its popup is stock's FRQ popup, so it reads in hertz where 0008 is built. RES sets the 2-pole types' Q, exponentially from RES 0: 0.707 to 2.0 for LP2 and HP2 (a peak up to +6.3 dB), 0.5 to 8 for BP, BS and PK (width only); LP1 and HP1 have none. DEP mixes the filtered voice with the dry one: 0 dB, then 0.25 dB steps of cut to -31.5 dB, then FULL, the plain filter. Below FULL, HP1 and HP2 give low shelves, LP1 and LP2 high shelves, BP cuts all but the band and BS is a bell cut of DEP's depth, the poles staying at FRQ. For PK, DEP is a boost instead, +0.0 to +6.0 dB over its range, built on BP. A slot's coefficients are worked out again only when its values change; switching between LP1 and HP1 at one FRQ carries the filter's state over (LP1 = x - HP1), so it should not click, but other type switches can. The TYP and RES knobs take stock TYP's and RES's encoder range and acceleration, copied into their records each idle tick, and TYP keeps its fractional delta, so both step as stock's. The 2-pole types run after the 1-pole pass, each slot on one of them through its biquad in place (direct form I, five multiplies a frame); a slot on none costs a few instructions a block, so the cost follows the voices using them. The coefficients are Q30, worked out in the interrupt when the slot's entry changes, from cos and sin of w0 per FRQ step (cave16), 1/a0 by divu.l and one Newton step; modelled against floating point over every type and FRQ, none is unstable and each lies within 3e-5 of its float design. The EMAC's << scale factor is not used: the first 2-pole build relied on it and BP came out silent and the other types wrong, as a model with the scale ignored predicts; Q30 products are now doubled after movclr, and the filter sums its terms at half scale and doubles with saturation. The DAC FILTER page's bottom row holds a transient shaper's ATK and SUS and POL. ATK and SUS run -64..+63, 0 the centre, drawn as SAMPLE FINE's dial (dotted at 0) and stepped as stock's PAN; FUNC + turn snaps to the next of -64, 0 and +63 once the turn adds up to `snap` steps one way. Full scale is 12 dB of attack or sustain change on a strong transient, the total boost capped at +6 dB. POL (+ or -) inverts the voice's contribution to the sum, folded into its pan gains, so it costs nothing; the individual outputs are untouched. The shaper runs after the filters and before the sum, a slot at a time for each voice whose track has ATK or SUS set. Once a block it takes the slot's peak and moves three followers - instant attack with 40 ms release, 15 ms attack with 150 ms release, instant attack with 300 ms release - and from dB(fast / slow) (the attack) and dB(hold / fast) (the sustain), each clipped to 12 dB, works out a gain, 0 dB below -60 dBFS. A block's own peak sets its gain (two passes: the peak, then the scaling), ramped from the last block's across it, or stepping there when it moves more than 3 dB, as at an onset. Levels in dB come from a normalisation and a 128-entry table, the gain from a 0.25 dB table, applied at half scale and doubled with saturation. A voice turned on starts its followers at its first block's peak. With ATK and SUS 0 on every voice track the shaper is skipped outright, a test a block (a flag the idle tick sets, so turning one on takes up to a tick); a voice at 0 among others is skipped and untouched. It was modelled in tools/voice_dac_shaper.py on captured voices first, and the device's integer code emulated against that model within 0.1 dB. Its knobs reuse ids 7 and 14 (Error records) and 457 (CB TEST's CB_OSC_SELECT, a hidden machine's, which stock never shows), renamed. The values are kept in the live sound's spare bytes, untagged: TYP in +0x6d bits 0-2, FRQ and DEP xor 0x7f in +0x6e/+0x6f, RES in velocity route 0's spare byte (below), so all zero is TYP OFF, FRQ 127, DEP FULL, RES 0; POL in +0x6d bit 3; ATK and SUS signed in velocity routes 1's and 2's spare bytes, clamped to -64..63 where read; +0x6d bits 4-7 and bit 7 of +0x6e and +0x6f are spare. sound_init_defaults and a load stock is about to fail clear them, so no sound reaches a track with them undefined; a sound reset resets DAC FILTER with the rest. TYP, FRQ, DEP and POL are saved in the stored record's spare slots 42 and 43 ((0xb8 + TYP) << 8 | FRQ, and POL << 8 | DEP), only when not all zero (sound-storage.md); a tick in the UI's idle routine copies each track's into the table the audio interrupt reads. TYP was renumbered to stock's order with the 2-pole types, so sounds saved before that load another type (LP1 as LP2, HP1 as LP1). Each change ends with the notice stock's sound settings setters send, SoundConfigChangedInfo through the track's sound accessor; without it a change played and survived a kit save but was lost at a reboot without one. The routes' spare bytes: each velocity and aftertouch route's amount word holds the amount in its high byte and, in stock, always 0 in its low byte - 64 bits a sound, for 0013's per-sound settings; velocity routes 0..2's hold RES, ATK and SUS, the other five are free. They are saved in slots 44..47 and loaded once sound_load has loaded the routes. Stock reads the whole word in three places, each hooked: the sound push clears the low byte on its way to the engine, and the route menus' models - SoundModConf (aftertouch) and Velocity, one template's two copies - clear it in getAmount, whose result the display rounds toward zero, and keep it in setAmount and setRoute, which write whole words. ControlInputParam, the template's third copy, holds the project's control inputs and is left alone. Hardware, 2026-10-07, POL in slot 43: POL - survives a reboot without a kit save, a kit save and reboot, the sound pool onto another track and NO + PLAY; a sound saved by the build before loads POL +. Before this, the save kept only TYP's bits of +0x6d and POL was lost at a reload or a reboot. Hardware, 2026-10-06, the shaper build: ATK and SUS shape onsets and tails as in the prototype, POL inverts, nothing is heard with both 0, values survive a reboot with and without a kit save, FUNC snaps, and the dial draws dotted at 0. Kits saved while the route-byte probe ran read ATK and SUS +63 (their marker, 90, clamped). Hardware, 2026-10-06, the 2-pole build: each type sounds as its glyph across FRQ; RES peaks LP2 and HP2 and narrows BP, BS and PK; DEP below FULL gives the shelves and BS's bell cut, PK's boost reading +0.0 to +6.0 dB; the bottom of the FRQ range is clean; TYP and RES survive a reboot with and without a kit save; TYP and RES step as stock's. Kits saved while the route-byte probe ran carry its marker, 0x5a, in every route byte: RES reads 90 on them. Hardware, 2026-10-06, dbg build: kits saved with the tagged bytes load the same values; untouched, stock-saved and reset sounds read the defaults; values survive a reboot with and without a kit save, the sound pool, copy/paste, NO + PLAY and a pattern change to another kit; the previous build reads kits this one saved. The route bytes' markers survive a kit save and reboot, amount edits, FUNC reset, destination changes and CLEAR/PASTE MODULATIONS and their UNDO in both menus, and no engine route word carried one. Hardware, 2026-09-29, DAC FILTER: TYP and DEP survive a reboot without a kit save (with the notice; not without it) and a kit save and reboot. An untouched sound reads DEP FULL (it read 0 dB while the default's DEP field was lost to a `|` the assembler takes as a comment). The screen is right: the popups (FRQ in hertz, DEP in dB and FULL, TYP), TYP's glyph and OFF, and the graph in the top row, flat in OFF. The rest of the HIGH-PASS list below: each mode sounds right across FRQ and DEP; the sound pool, copy/paste, NO + PLAY kit reload and a pattern change to another kit and back are not yet checked for this version. DAC SUM, the last item of AUDIO ROUTING, switches it at run time. OFF is stock's routing and no sum. It is kept with the project's globals, beside the routing it overrides: stored bytes +12 (tag) and +13 of each of the four projectGlobalsStorage_v2_t records, which stock's load and save never touch. Each record keeps its own value; the UI's idle tick follows the active one. A record saved without the tag loads as OFF. The item is built after USB TO MAIN with USB OUT's sequence and managers; its value draws as ON or OFF and changes with the value controls, up for ON. Switching clicks once: the analog bus changes at once, the DAC path 2.58 ms later. Hardware, 2026-09-28, the HIGH-PASS version this page replaced (one knob, HPF), with the shipping mods: the page shows only while DAC SUM is on, the knob and its popup work, each track keeps its own value, and 0004's LFO RND and 0008's FRQ popup are unaffected. The value survives kit save and reload, another kit loaded and back, a pattern change to another kit and back, NO + PLAY kit reload, the sound pool, sound copy/paste and a power cycle - with a kit save before it, as that version wrote the sound without the change notice; an untouched sound reads OFF. Muted tracks go silent with DAC SUM on as with it off. DAC SUM survives power cycles, on and off, without a project save. CPU, 2026-10-06, the burn build (tools/voice_dac_burn.py) with 0006's telemetry, in the worst case: A16 playing, DAC SUM on, every voice track LP1, the compressor preview page up. With nothing added 0013 took 4.24% of a block, the UI event queue held at about 2, BgWorker had jobs pending in every frame and 0006's estimator stood aside in every frame. Added interrupt time did not make the queue run away: each step raised it to a new level it then held for the minute - about 20 at +0.5%, 59 at +1%, 104 at +1.5%, 147 at +2% - so the UI kept up but further behind, and the preview page's scrolling visibly paused from +0.5%. An earlier 10 s sweep without a drain between steps read that climb as a runaway; at +8% the device's USB audio dropped and it needed a reboot. Where the UI stops answering lies above +2%, not measured. New per-voice stages cost in proportion to the voices using them, as each is skipped when off; this worst case is not the one to size them against. Headroom, 2026-09-28, the timing build's peak and clip counters over A01-A16 and B01-B05 with DAC SUM on and every HPF off (build/mix/20260928_145359, tools/voice_dac_headroom.py): the DAC sum, PRE returns included, peaked at -12.3 dBFS at most (A16; -21.6 at least, A09), and no side-frame reached full scale on any pattern. The filter skips a pair of slots that are both off (TYP OFF or DEP 0 dB), keeping its state on the signal so turning a filter on does not click (by ear, 2026-09-28, HIGH-PASS version). From the profile, that took the stub from about 3.2% of a block to about 1.6% with no HPF engaged, about 0.4% a pair engaged. The DAC FILTER version, timing build, 2026-09-29, one session, all eight voices playing: 2.44% of a block (median; 2.87% p99) with every TYP OFF, 3.96% (4.26% p99, 4.48% max) with every voice track LP1 - 0.38% a pair, as the HIGH-PASS filter's. Coefficients are worked out only when a slot's values change, so the steady state adds a compare a slot. The route byte's only other writers are analog circuit calibration's, which only ever take voices off the bus (compressor-hardware.md), so nothing puts the analog path back under the DAC path. Hardware, 2026-09-28, before the switch: the voices sounded right, the pan split matched stock within 0.01 per slot over USB, the latency was 2.58 ms and the polarity was inverted, since fixed. K and the slot trims were then set from A/Bs on and off: slots 0-3 and 5 match the analog path within 0.1 dB; slot 6's trim was corrected from the same measurement and not measured again. Known limits: the voices reach MAIN 2.58 ms later than they would through the analog bus. They share the PRE pair with the delay and reverb returns and the PRE-FX audio input, and are clamped at its full scale (about 12 dB above the loudest pattern measured). Individual outputs are unaffected, and carry the voice before the filter. TYP, FRQ and DEP cannot be p-locked or reached over MIDI: they live outside the sound's 42 parameters. Switching TYP between LP1 and HP1 clicks on a sound with much energy at either end (hardware, 2026-09-29): the state carries over, but the output changes from one filter's to the other's at once; a crossfade would take it away. The graph draws LP1's slope right of the FRQ point and HP1's left of it, as stock's FILTER graph does. The slot 4 and 7 trims rest on one pattern each. With DAC SUM on the USB voice channels carry the filtered voices. Port of rytm-mods 0013-voice-dac.
